core_rules: brownfield register entry is not planning permission
Part 1 brownfield register status must not be treated as Part 2 permission in principle
Part 2 permission in principle still requires technical details consent before development
brownfield deliverable flag is not a guaranteed construction start or completion date
planning-permission-status must be read with an effective date and current authority record
permissioned status is not evidence that development has commenced
not-permissioned status is not evidence that the site is unsuitable for development
pending-decision status is not an approval
permission in principle is limited to its legal scope and cannot be treated as full permission
full planning permission, outline permission, reserved matters, permission in principle and technical details consent must remain distinct
ownership-status is a category and not definitive proof of legal title
unknown ownership must not be converted into public or private ownership
site-category vocabulary must not be treated as a parcel development conclusion
experimental brownfield-site geometry must not override authoritative brownfield-land records
authoritative platform origin does not remove the need for current local-authority readback when status can change
brownfield register review cadence means stale entries require revalidation before use
record end-date must be respected and ended records must not be promoted as current opportunities
development-complete notes must cause current-growth promotion to fail closed
minimum and maximum dwelling counts are capacity estimates, not development entitlements
hectares in a register are not necessarily the exact developable parcel area
greenfield land within a mixed site must not be treated as brownfield merely because the wider site appears on a register
EIA and habitats constraints can prevent permission in principle and require exact legal checks
local development plan policies and material considerations still apply after permission in principle
technical details consent must not be inferred from permission in principle
SHLAA or SHELAA inclusion is evidence gathering, not allocation or planning permission
land availability assessment suitability, availability and achievability are assessment concepts rather than consent
Housing Delivery Test is authority-level delivery evidence and not parcel-level growth evidence
Housing Delivery Test 2023 covers 2020/21, 2021/22 and 2022/23 and must remain period exact
absence of a newer published Housing Delivery Test must not be replaced with an assumed 2024 or 2025 result
Housing Delivery Test percentage is delivered homes divided by required homes over the defined measurement period
local housing need is an unconstrained minimum need figure and is not itself the adopted housing requirement
five-year housing land supply is an authority-level supply assessment and not an individual parcel permission
NPPF deliverable years 1-5 and developable years 6-10 or 11-15 must remain conceptually distinct
five-year supply buffers must be date-versioned and the 1 July 2026 policy condition must not be backdated
housing-land-supply templates are evidence presentation tools and not adopted policy or inspector findings
new plan-making system guidance that is marked draft must not be treated as final immutable policy
local plan examination activity is not evidence that a plan has been adopted
brownfield passport working-paper proposals must not be treated as enacted planning law
Brownfield Infrastructure and Land Fund availability or support is not proof of funding for a specific parcel
funding eligibility is not a funding award
funding award is not planning permission
funding award is not construction completion
Homes England due diligence or land support is not proof of title, viability or deliverability
Building for a Healthy Life is a design assessment toolkit and not planning permission
London SHLAA informs strategic housing capacity and targets but does not itself grant permission
local-authority SHLAA inclusion must not be promoted without current policy and application evidence
point coordinates from a site record are not exact cadastral boundaries
site-plan links must be inspected before geometry is used for canonical parcel intersection
provider count and collector-run date are platform metadata and not individual-site effective dates
entry-date must not be confused with planning-permission date, commencement date or completion date
planning-permission date must not be treated as evidence of commencement or completion
dwellings capacity values must not be downscaled or upscaled into a guaranteed parcel yield
brownfield register inclusion must not be treated as proof that remediation costs or infrastructure constraints are solved
no current platform record is NO_DATA and not evidence that no brownfield site exists
absence from the experimental brownfield-site layer is not evidence of absence from an authoritative local register
duplicate official pages carrying the same underlying record count as one evidence family
research-source confidence is not parcel-level accuracy
RECOVERY_PARKED forbids parcel relation creation, Future Growth scoring and business-row promotion
predecessor height_difference_2 must not be bypassed
second shared runner must not be created while canonical recovery remains unresolved
research-only web publication may continue only with explicit fail-closed promotion guards
